title: Continue-link email builds tokenized resume/erasure URLs from attacker-influenceable X-Forwarded-Host (*.run.app allowlist arm)
evidence:
Ok(pog.Returned(_, [row, ..])) -> {
                      let origin = http_origin.canonical_origin(req)
                      let base = origin <> "/apply/" <> vacancy.short_code
                      case
                        email_client.send_draft_continue_link(
                          config.resend_api_key,
                          applicant_email,
                          vacancy.property_name,
                          base <> "/resume/" <> row.continue_token,
                          base <> "/draft-erasure/" <> row.continue_token,

-- server/src/http_origin.gleam:32-58:
  let raw =
    request.get_header(req, "x-forwarded-host")
    |> result.try_recover(fn(_) { request.get_header(req, "host") })
...
    || string.ends_with(host, ".run.app")

-- server/src/middleware.gleam:286 (is_public_path, skips X-RT-Secret):
    ["apply", _, "continue-link"] -> True
detail: Emailed continue/erasure URLs derive from the request origin; http_origin trusts any *.run.app X-Forwarded-Host and the endpoint is public. An attacker (owning any free .run.app host) poisons the origin; the victim's genuine branded email carries their live 288-bit token to the attacker's domain — one click exposes saved application PII (read via resume, delete via erasure).
recommended_fix: Build the emailed base from vacancy.origin_domain via email_client.build_entity_url (the confirmation-email /erase/ link precedent at application_handler.gleam:2122), never from request headers; reserve canonical_origin for response-local canonical tags.
